paras: The killing of Charlie at Kissimmee was the fatal shooting of a Black man known only as Charlie by W. A. Patterson in Kissimmee, Florida, on Saturday, August 15, 1885. Patterson accused Charlie of trying to "outrage" his sister, shot him as he fled, and surrendered; a justice's jury found the killing justifiable the same evening.

Charlie had been hired for a few days by the elder Patterson, a storekeeper at the Bartow junction of the South Florida railroad, and slept in the kitchen of the family's house. The father testified that on the Thursday night he woke to a scream from his daughter Katie and saw Charlie get off the foot of her bed and run into the kitchen.

About 4 o'clock on Saturday, pistol shots drew Mayor J. W. Aderhold from a drug store, and a young man named W. A. Patterson told him he had killed a negro and wanted to give himself up. "I have followed him here and have killed him," Patterson said; "I ask to be protected by the law." According to the dispatch, Charlie ran from a store toward a swamp when he saw Patterson, who fired three times; the body lay face down with a bullet hole in the back of the head.

The mayor turned Patterson over to the marshal, and the father and Katie Patterson arrived by train that evening. Justice J. E. Sites impaneled a jury, which viewed the body and heard the father and Katie; the jurors "were out just long enough to write a verdict of justifiable homicide." No report of a grand jury or trial was found, and Charlie's full name does not appear in the coverage.

The only known report ran on August 20 in the Savannah Morning News as a Kissimmee dispatch dated August 16. Its headline, "KISSIMMEE'S TRAGEDY," and subhead, "Young Patterson Acquired [acquitted] for Shooting the Negro Who Assaulted His Sister," stated the family's accusation as fact. The story gave only the Pattersons' version and nothing from or about Charlie beyond his first name; no coverage was found in the Black press.

reader.title: Killing of Charlie at Kissimmee
bases: A single man, W. A. Patterson, pursued and shot Charlie on his own after a private accusation, with no mob, band, posse or officers involved (A2).
The only report is one Kissimmee dispatch in the Savannah Morning News (A2); no other white or Black paper was found.

accounts.label: Killer's statement to the mayor
accounts.gist: Patterson said Charlie had tried to outrage his sister the previous Thursday night, that he had followed him to Kissimmee and killed him, and that he wanted the law's protection.

accounts.label: Father's testimony at the inquest
accounts.gist: The elder Patterson testified he woke to Katie's scream, saw Charlie get off the foot of her bed and run into the kitchen, and that Charlie left his hat behind; Katie corroborated.

accounts.label: Dispatch's narrative of the shooting
accounts.gist: Patterson found Charlie in a store; Charlie ran out a side door toward a swamp; Patterson fired three times and the jury found the body face down with a bullet hole in the back of the head.

framing.detail: The Savannah Morning News headed the dispatch "KISSIMMEE'S TRAGEDY" with a subhead stating Patterson shot "the Negro Who Assaulted His Sister," taking the family's accusation as fact and printing only the Pattersons' testimony.

record_check.dossier: Attempted outrage (sexual assault) on Katie Patterson, alleged by her brother and father
pursuit and shooting; three shots fired, one striking the back of the head
Charlie was at large, fleeing; not in custody
Revenge for the alleged attempted outrage on Patterson's sister

record_check.record: a jury returned a verdict in his favor
record_check.dossier: The jury was an inquest jury impaneled by Justice J. E. Sites the same day; its verdict was justifiable homicide. No report of a grand jury or trial was found.

info: Saturday, August 15, 1885, about 4 o'clock ("Last Saturday" in a dispatch dated Sunday, Aug. 16)
Kissimmee: in and outside a store, as Charlie ran toward a large swamp
A Black man ("the negro") known to the Patterson family only as Charlie, hired for a few days by the elder Patterson

Accused by the Pattersons of trying to "outrage" Miss Katie Patterson in her bed at the family's house at the Bartow junction of the South Florida railroad between 2 and 3 a.m. on the preceding Thursday night
W. A. Patterson, a young man, brother of Katie Patterson, of the Bartow junction of the South Florida railroad
The jury returned a verdict of justifiable homicide; the headline says Patterson was "Acquired" [acquitted]

sources.note: Kissimmee, Fla., dispatch of Aug. 16: W. A. Patterson shot dead a Black man known only as Charlie whom he accused of trying to outrage his sister; Justice Sites's jury found justifiable homicide.
quotes: Young Patterson Acquired for Shooting the Negro Who Assaulted His Sister.
We know him only as Charlie. Last Thursday night he tried to outrage my sister, Miss Katie Patterson. I have followed him here and have killed him. I ask to be protected by the law.
The jury found the negro lying on his face with a bullet hole in the back of his head.
he ran through a side door in the direction of a large swamp. Mr. Patterson followed and shot at him three times, one shot taking effect.
The jury were out just long enough to write a verdict of justifiable homicide.
